title: fix(runtime): a sandboxed body whose rejection no read can flatten ends its run at once with a fixed sentence, instead of at the wall-clock ceiling (#23723)
body:
Fixes #23723
Clause-②: no

## What changed

A sandboxed body whose rejection no read can flatten now ends its run at once, on the same "threw" path as any other rejection, with the fixed sentence `the script threw a value that could not be read`. Before, it waited for the wall-clock ceiling (30 s at the action door) and the door answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, naming no refusal.

One writer, `REJECT_HANDLER` in `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts`:

- The fallback read (`(e && e.message) ? (e.name + ': ' + e.message) : String(e)`) used to run outside any `try`. A `message` getter that throws, or a null-prototype object whose `String()` throws, threw out of the handler there, so `__error` stayed unset; `throw ''` set it to `''`. The pump loop ends a run only on a non-empty `__error`, so neither ended.
- The fallback expression is unchanged, now inside a `try`. When no read yields a non-empty string, the handler records `Error: ` + the fixed sentence (a module constant, `UNREADABLE_REJECTION_SENTENCE`). `userFacingMessage` strips the `Error: ` name as for any thrown `Error`, so the sentence is the `innerMessage`.
- The two side channels after it (`__errorInfo`, `__errorRefusal`) are untouched. They now also run for these values, because the handler no longer throws before them. So a `code` on such a value is kept, as for any other thrown value.
- The pump loop is unchanged (hypothesis H3 holds: the handler can always set a non-empty `__error`, so no "rejected but unrecorded" case is needed there).
- No door, no export, no status mapping, no envelope key, no `packages/spec` file.

The sentence names nothing the value carried (the getter's own error is not read into it) and no stack.

## Before / after, measured

Rig: a temporary probe (deleted before any commit), run at base `2906cd8d2e` and at the fix commit `eba201b22`. Runner rows use a `QuickJSScriptRunner` with a 3000 ms ceiling (CPU budget the same). Door rows are `POST /api/v1/actions/:object/:action` on `type: 'script'` actions, PR #23722's rig: better-sqlite3 `:memory:` under the real `ObjectQL`, bodies bound through `actionBodyRunnerFactory` over a default `QuickJSScriptRunner` (30 s ceiling), `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` over a real Fetch `Request`. Wall-clock figures are from a shared box.

| body throws | at the runner, before | at the runner, after | at the door, before | at the door, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{ code: 'EMAIL_TAKEN', get message() { throw new Error('boom') } }` | 3014 ms, budget error `exceeded wall-clock ceiling of 3000ms while awaiting host calls`, no `innerMessage`, no `code` | 23 ms, `action 'submit' threw: Error: the script threw a value that could not be read`, `innerMessage` the sentence, `code` `EMAIL_TAKEN` | 30117 ms, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` `Internal server error` | 108 ms, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `declaredCode` `EMAIL_TAKEN`, the sentence |
| the same, hook origin | 3013 ms, budget error | 9 ms, `hook 'submit' threw: Error: …`, the sentence, `EMAIL_TAKEN` | not measured | not measured |
| `''` | 3025 ms, budget error | 34 ms, the sentence | 30104 ms, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` | 118 ms, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, the sentence |
| `Object.create(null)` | 3014 ms, budget error | 28 ms, the sentence | 30116 ms, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` | 116 ms, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, the sentence |
| an `Error` whose `name` and `message` are both empty | 3111 ms, budget error | 131 ms, the sentence | 30142 ms, `500` | 109 ms, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, the sentence |
| an `Error` whose `message` getter throws | 3009 ms, budget error | 9 ms, the sentence | 30116 ms, `500` | 114 ms, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, the sentence |
| CONTROL: a body that never settles | 3014 ms, budget error | 3010 ms, budget error (unchanged) | 30129 ms, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` | 30101 ms, `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` (unchanged) |

The door's status for these values is the one it already gives a body that threw a value with no registered code (`throw {}` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before and after). It was measured, not changed.

The last two value rows are not in the card. They are the same defect (a read that throws, or a `String()` that is empty), found while reading the handler, and they move inside triage's scope ("Any rejection is recorded, even when reading it throws or yields `''`").

## Unchanged answers, byte-compared

The probe recorded every value the handler could already read, at the runner (`ctor`, `name`, `message`, `innerMessage`, `code`, `status`, `fields`, `userMessage` of the error) and at the door (status and full response body), before and after. **39 of 39 rows are byte-identical** (18 runner rows, 21 door rows):

- PR #23722's plain objects: `{ code, message }`, `{ code }`, `{ code, status: 409, message }`, `{}`, `[]`, `{ name: 'TypeError', message }`, a `message` starting `Error: `, an own `toString`;
- a real `Error`, `TypeError`, an `Error` carrying a code, an `Error` with no message carrying a code;
- the `__errorInfo` channel (`code`, `fields`, `status: 422`, `userMessage`);
- primitives: a string, `null`, `undefined`, `0`, `false`;
- at the door only: the engine refusal PR #23717 relays (`409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION` with `details`), a nested hook refusal's sentence through the `__errorRefusal` channel (`400 VALIDATION_ERROR` `x`), and a capability denial (`500 INTERNAL_ERROR`).

## Tests

- `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/unreadable-rejection-recorded.test.ts` (new, 8): the three shapes, the getter shape on the hook origin, the two extra `Error` shapes; CONTROLS: `{ code, message }` keeps PR #23722's answer, and a never-settling body still ends at the ceiling with no `innerMessage`.
- `packages/runtime/src/sandbox-unreadable-rejection-door.test.ts` (new, 5): the three shapes at the action door (status, `code`, `declaredCode`, sentence); CONTROLS: `{ code, message }` keeps PR #23722's answer, and a never-settling body still answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`.
- Both use a runner with a 1000 ms wall ceiling (CPU budget the same). A named refusal from it is an answer within a second by construction, and a regression is the ceiling's budget error at that second, never a 30 s wait or a clock assertion.
- The sentence is the ruled one, so it is asserted exactly, beside the code and status.

The anchor (the new guarded `try` and the last-resort assignment, 4 lines) was replaced by the base's one-line assignment plus a marker: anchor 1 to 0, marker 0 to 1, blob `9870e8bc5b0c` to `5569a01b0649`. Run over the two new files plus PR #23722's unit pin: `Tests 9 failed | 14 passed (23)`. Exactly the 9 shape rows went red (6 unit rows received `exceeded wall-clock ceiling of 1000ms …`, 3 door rows received `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`); all 4 controls and PR #23722's 10 rows stayed green. ## Gates

At `f7ddaeb73`, `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 61 commands from 4 changed paths (merge base `140238a47`). All 61 ran, each exit code captured to a file before any pipe.

- 60 answered exit 0 on the first pass.
- `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` answered exit 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (no workspace `dist`). After a full turbo build (75 tasks, 74 cached; the runtime `dist` carries the new sentence, grep count 1 in `index.js` and in `index.cjs`) it answered exit 0: `110 published require entry point(s) across 68 package(s) load`.
- `--ran`: `61 derived, 61 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`, exit 0.

- `--format json` over the three changed `.ts` files: 0 errors, 0 warnings each. The changeset is outside the linted path.
- Positive control: a root `@objectstack/spec` import on stdin at a `packages/runtime` path, exit 1, `no-restricted-imports`.

CI's families are this PR's check-runs; none was re-run locally.

## Acceptance notes

- In-process: a caller that catches the `SandboxError` for such a throw now gets `KIND 'NAME' threw: Error: the script threw a value that could not be read` with that sentence as `innerMessage`, instead of the budget error. The changeset states it.
- A value that answered at once before keeps its answer byte for byte (above). Only values whose every read threw or was empty move.
